What RawBars is

@@ -75,6 +85,26 @@ const t = (s) => s; which buy back the brevity. They all share one engine, prelude, and compiler — they differ only in surface syntax.

+ +
+

Four words this site uses precisely:

+
+
Core
+
the meaning-free parser (the flatbars package). It gives a tag + structure, never meaning. RawBars is the core's bare surface.
+
Surface
+
the syntax you write. FlatBars has four: RawBars ⊂ FullBars ⊂ MaxBars form the + dialect ladder (each adds sugar over the same core); MinBars is a + Mustache-compatible peer.
+
Engine
+
the runtime that assigns meaning — operations, scope, truthiness. The FlatBars + dialects share one.
+
Operation (host API: helper)
+
the named thing a tag applies; there are no variables, so even + {t("{{{city}}}")} applies the operation city. The JS host API + keeps the word helper (registerHelper).
+

Where to go next

+

+ You rarely write RawBars by hand — it's the substrate you target. For everyday + templating, climb the ladder: MinBars is the + logic-less on-ramp, FullBars adds Handlebars-style blocks + and helpers, and MaxBars adds infix operators and pipes — + all desugaring to the core you just saw. To compute a value before rendering, see + Data shaping. Or open the bare core in the + Lab. +
